hypotheses.claim: For binary/bin-packing instances on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 style data, a score_item that is monotone decreasing in item size (plus a tie-break term favouring items that fill the residual capacity of an open bin most tightly) yields strictly lower bin count than insertion order or random order at a 500 ms budget, because large items have the fewest feasible placements and must be placed while slack is still large; the repack pass then recovers the residual waste that a pure FFD ordering leaves.

next_search_advice.direction: Implement `rank_items(items, capacity, ctx)` so the offline reorder+repack template places items in non-increasing size order (First-Fit-Decreasing style), breaking ties by descending remainder-fit to the current open bin, then run greedy FFD packing and attempt a local repack of partially filled bins.
